title: Keychain credentials may be extractable on compromised device
description: AuthStore.swift persists GatewayCredentials with kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly. Credentials are accessible after device unlock; on a compromised device, tokens may be extracted via Keychain dumps.
root_cause: Keychain item accessibility class may not provide sufficient protection beyond device passcode.
intended_behavior: Credentials should be protected by stronger accessibility (e.g. kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly or biometric-protected storage) for high-value tokens.

conditions.description: Device compromised or passcode guessed; no additional app-level encryption.

execution.attacker_perspective: No live exploitation; state pollution only affects local client's subsequent auth flows.
instructions: Source review complete; verify accessibility attribute value matches intended policy.
execution.observed_result: Source review confirms kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly used for stored credentials.

remediation.strategy: Consider stronger Keychain accessibility for high-value tokens (e.g. kSecAttrAccessibleWhenPasscodeSetThisDeviceOnly or biometric-protected storage).

likelihood.reason: Requires device compromise or passcode guessing.

impact.reason: No credential exposure at rest; only Keychain accessibility.

title: PKCE state not cleared when OAuth/ASWebAuthenticationSession is cancelled
description: HermesAuthenticator stores PKCE verifier and active provider (activePKCE, activeProvider) in startNousOAuth()/startOIDCAuth() and clears them only in completeOAuth(); the ASWebAuthenticationSession cancel path returns early without clearing them.
claimed_root_cause: Cancellation path in AuthView.presentOAuth returns early without clearing activePKCE/activeProvider.

trace.description: ASWebAuthenticationSession completion handler invoked; .canceledLogin branch at 268-269 returns at 270-272.
Only removal of activePKCE/activeProvider (repo-wide search: 4 references total); unreachable on cancel.

evidence.description: Actual cancel handler (original claim cited line 254; that line is a comment).

reason: No security boundary is crossed. activePKCE is never read in the codebase and never transmitted; the authorization-code token exchange is server-side (comment 291-301), so no verifier leaves the device. activeProvider is only read at line 318 as a label fallback and is overwritten by any subsequent start* call before completeOAuth is reachable. A stale in-process value that is never transmitted and never observed by another principal is a robustness/UX nit (severity informational at best), not a vulnerability. Independent verifier (fresh source-reading agent, subagent id sa-0-4cd1a811) confirmed all 4 references and the non-security impact.

title: OAuth authorization request missing anti-CSRF `state` parameter; never validated on callback
description: Both OAuth flows (startNousOAuth lines 235-243; startOIDCAuth 277-284) build authorization URLs without a `state` parameter. completeOAuth (297-331) captures session cookie from dashboard /auth/callback but never validates a returned `state` value. Per OAuth 2.0 BCP (RFC 6749 §10.12), missing `state` removes anti-CSRF protection on the authorization request.
claimed_root_cause: Authorization URL construction omits `state`; callback never validates it.

evidence.description: startNousOAuth — authorization URL construction, no state parameter.
completeOAuth — callback handler never validates state.

blockers: Server-side OAuth state-validation policy and gateway token-exchange behavior not visible in this repository; practical exploitability requires server-side confirmation (token exchange and authorization endpoint behavior are server-side). Source review completed by independent verifier; deployment/server-side validation required.

validation_plan.local: Confirm source absence; add state-generation code in start* flows; add validation in completeOAuth.
validation_plan.deployment: Verify gateway server validates `state` during token exchange; confirm no server-side state bypass; test authorization-request CSRF resistance against deployed gateway.

title: Failed WS ticket minting silently proceeds to unauthenticated dial
description: mintWSTicket() in HermesAuthenticator.swift returns nil on any failure (non-200 HTTP, missing ticket JSON, network error); AuthGateView.authenticate() consumes the result before connecting.
claimed_root_cause: mintWSTicket swallows errors with try? and returns nil; callers do not surface ticket-minting failure.

trace.description: Guard checks mint result; on nil sets errorMessage = "Failed to mint WebSocket ticket" and returns (lines 68-74).
No WebSocket dial with a nil ticket; user sees an error message.

evidence.description: authenticate() guards the mint result and surfaces a user-visible error instead of dialing.

reason: The claim that a failed mint leads to a silent unauthenticated dial is refuted by source: AuthGateView.authenticate() (lines 66-74) uses guard let ... else { errorMessage = "Failed to mint WebSocket ticket"; return }, which prevents GatewayConnection.connect() from ever being called with a nil or failed ticket. No weaker fallback auth path or stale-credential cache exists in the code. Independent verifier (subagent id sa-1-3db160de) confirmed the guard and absence of a fallback path. The behavior is an availability/UX issue (errors are not differentiated), not a security boundary violation.
